pattern: The 14 wrong runs split into 6 wrong answers, 5 budget exhaustions and 3 provider-stall timeouts. There were no search failures: 13 of 14 runs displayed and fully read the gold body; the exception is Haiku OVERLOAD, which saw only hexToLong's signature. (1) Chart definer family, 4 answered plus 3 Sonnet budget runs. Every answer ranked PlotUtilities.drift first, and every no-answer run had already committed to drift ('should be point2 - point1'). Each run derived the drift convention from the expected 87.5. All caller greps were scoped to source/, so PlotUtilitiesTests.testDrift was never fetched. This includes the one run that actually executed the test and saw 87.5 vs 112.5 (opus55t). These are convention priors left uncorrected because the evidence was never retrieved, not attribution from a misread body. (2) Lang MASK. Both answered Sonnet runs did retrieve the production second caller BitField.setValue, but misread it ('works correctly because index=0'). Run-016 even said setValue 'looks correct' because the mask is pre-positioned, yet both kept overlay first and the rest in strict depth order. These are evidence-integration failures, not retrieval failures. (3) No-answer runs are dominated by infrastructure. defects4j test fails with a missing String::Interpolate Perl module in every Haiku and Sonnet run, and agents spent many steps on mvn/ant/javac workarounds. The 3 timeouts (LEX-006, MASK-004, CONV-013) each show about 4 minutes of silence after the last tool output. At least one stalled run (LEX-006) had already traced the gold's p=256. One budget run (Haiku DEPTH) had marked the decoy overlay as the primary bug in its working file.
